global_caption: The video contains 5 shots and is a realistic-style multi-person It employs a neutral color palette and cold metallic textures, enhanced by faint edge lighting from the starfield visible through the viewport. The camera movement is controlled and oppressive, using only Spanish The
shot1: Shot 1 serves as the opening shot, establishing the space with a wide overhead view. The composition emphasizes the central authority position via the circular seating arrangement and converging lines of sight. The primary lighting inside the chamber is uniform cold neutral top light, with slight backlight outlining the viewport edges. The presiding eagle stands before the high seat, wings tucked, chest raised, adjusting his metallic claws before lifting the gavel. " The gavel strike drowns out the previously low-level murmurs in the chamber. The camera slightly pushes in at the moment of impact, reinforcing the ceremonial nature of the opening.
shot2: Shot 2 connects to the previous shot with a hard cut, cutting to a medium-close eye-level side-angle reverse shot. The foreground is softly blurred, showing the edge of the tribunal bench, with focus locked on the prosecution eagle’s profile and sharp beak. In the background, the curved wall and seat silhouettes of the tribunal chamber are visible. Shallow depth of field highlights the speaker. Lighting remains in cold neutral tone, with only faint viewport reflection on the beak edge. The prosecution eagle leans forward, wings pressed against the table edge, neck extending toward the defendant’s bench. " When stressing key words, the lower beak closes more decisively. The camera performs a slight horizontal pan, following his forward-leaning pressure motion, while capturing brief glances from other eagles in the frame edge.
shot3: It cuts to a close-up eye-level over-the-shoulder shot from behind the prosecution eagle, looking toward the defense eagle. The starfield through the viewport creates a calm and vast depth in the background. The same neutral metallic lighting is used, supplemented by faint starlight edge illumination. The defense eagle first turns his head from the table toward the viewport, then quickly returns to center, raising wingtips in a stopping gesture. After a brief pause, his beak opens and closes methodically, delivering "Objeción, no es concluyente. The prosecution eagle remains stiff and reserved in the foreground. Low murmurs in the chamber rise slightly before being suppressed again. The camera performs a very light push-in to emphasize the strength of the objection.
shot4: Shot 4 transitions from the previous shot with a brief fade cut, shifting to a medium low-angle shot with slight tilt. The camera moves closer to the hatch area, with the foreground showing a partially open mechanical door frame and a strip of cold white light from the gap. The witness eagle standing beside the door becomes the visual focal point. In the background, seats and blurred audience silhouettes along the circular wall are visible. Lighting continues the cold neutral tone, but side lighting from the door enhances feather texture and tense expression. The camera performs a very light upward tilt and push-in, elevating the importance of the testimony.
shot5: Shot 5 returns to the authoritative perspective with a hard cut from the previous shot, using a composite staging of wide to medium-close. It begins with a level-wide shot re-establishing the positions of the four eagles in the circular tribunal chamber, then slowly pushes in toward the presiding eagle’s close-up. The foreground sweeps past several chair backs to create spatial layering, while the starfield in the background viewport remains stable under cold light. The composition centers again on the high seat. Overall lighting remains unchanged, with only the presiding eagle’s face and beak receiving more concentrated top lighting. He first surveys the room, sharp eyes scanning the prosecution, defense, and witness. The entire chamber returns to an oppressive silence. Then he leans forward slightly, his beak opening and closing steadily and deeply, precisely delivering "El tribunal deliberará. " As the final word lands, the camera completes its push-in and briefly holds still.
